title: Ephemeral API key tenant misbind after leader swap in private VPC with mTLS and sticky sessions
creator: Maya Chen
description: Production customer (large financial client on Private VPC) reported intermittent 403s and tenant misattribution following a control-plane leader election and a concurrent API key rotation. Symptoms only appeared for clients using mutual TLS + sticky session enabled on their ingress. The issue manifests as requests authenticated with a newly minted ephemeral API key being evaluated against the prior node's tenant binding, producing either cross-tenant rejection or, in rarer cases, transient access to stale tenant scopes. This ticket tracks investigation, a hotfix, customer mitigation, and postmortem.
impact_summary: A single customer experienced elevated 403 rates (10-15% of requests) for ~18 minutes during a scheduled control-plane leader failover. Impact included production outages for several internal services that rely on correct org-scoped API key validation. Rollback to stable routing reduced errors. Potential exposure: transient misbinding of session to an old tenant mapping while key rotation was in-flight. No confirmed data exfiltration, but high availability and authorization correctness were impacted.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Setup Private deployment with sticky-session enabled on ingress and mTLS between edge and inference nodes.
2) Start a long-lived session bound to tenant A using an ephemeral API key.
3) Trigger control-plane leader election (simulate node restart or failover) while simultaneously rotating ephemeral API keys for tenant A.
4) Observe that some requests post-rotation are evaluated against stale tenant bindings (tenant B) or rejected with 403 although API key is valid.
Notes: Reproducible in staging when timing window aligns; requires sticky-session cookie to be present so inbound stickyness hides upstream reroute.
Helpful debug flags: ENABLE_AUTH_TRACE=1, DEBUG_KV_CACHE=1 on affected nodes.
initial_findings: Auth cache (local tenant binding cache + ephemeral API key index) was not fully invalidated on leader-change events under sticky-session routing. Edge continued routing a subset of connections to the old worker where in-memory binding state differed from control-plane's new mapping during rotation. The combination of sticky sessions (keeping connections attached to a worker) and asynchronous key rotation created a race: the worker accepted the rotated key but used an outdated tenant pointer from its ephemeral cache. This is a design flaw in the tenant-binding lifecycle during leader handoff.
mitigation_taken: 1) Immediate config change for the customer: disabled sticky-session at ingress and forced full connection drain during leader swap (customer-approved). 2) Short-lived rollback of the new rotation window by pausing automatic ephemeral key rollouts for the customer's org. 3) Deployed a hotfix that forces tenant-binding cache invalidation on leader election and during key-roll events (hotfix candidate PR linked).
fix_and_prs: PR: github.com/redwood-inference/platform/pull/9827 - add integration tests for sticky-session + key-rotation race
postmortem_actions: 1) Ensure control plane broadcasts authoritative tenant-binding epochs and workers must confirm epoch sync before accepting rotated keys (owner: Diego Morales, due: 2026-03-01).
2) Add e2e test covering sticky sessions + leader-change + key rotation to catch regressions (owner: Priya Patel, estimate: 3).
3) Improve observability: add metric auth.cache_epoch_mismatch and alert at >1/minute per node (owner: Liam O'Connor, due: 2026-02-25).
4) Update runbooks to recommend disabling sticky sessions during large-scale rotations and to drain connections pre-failover (owner: SRE team).
